subject: Repository activity must not imply deployment

naya.understanding: A Git-connected Vercel project was automatically producing deployments for repository changes that were documentation, notes, specifications, and governance artifacts. This exposed an architectural boundary defect: source activity was implicitly coupled to publication.
naya.lesson: CONNECTED != DEPLOYABLE. A repository change is not a release. Deployment is a privileged side effect that requires explicit authorization, exact commit binding, verification evidence, target environment, and approval.
naya.next_action: Maintain the fail-closed deployment governance contract and verify provider behavior with current Vercel evidence whenever a release or configuration change occurs.

human.meaning: NayaPOWER should stay connected to Vercel, but adding or changing files must not instantly publish or deploy the work. Vercel should be a deployment target, not the automatic destination of every repository action.
human.decision: Adopt an explicit release gate while preserving the Vercel connection.

provenance.source: User-observed Vercel deployment behavior plus current repository/Vercel inspection
provenance.triggering_observation: Introduce NayaNet and Collective Chain Technology caused a Vercel production deployment from main.
evidence: Vercel project naya-power is Git-connected to SoulSchoolAcademy/NayaPOWER
Vercel deployment history contains repeated deployments for documentation, Smart Note, CCT, and ordinary repository changes
NayaPOWER previously had no vercel.json deployment gate

verification.receipt: Repository-side configuration and fail-closed tests were added. External provider non-deployment behavior requires fresh post-change Vercel observation.
